sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Greenup County, KY?
sections.html:
The Sheriff's Office collects tax bills, the PVA assesses, and the County Clerk takes over after April 15. All three work out of the Greenup County Courthouse area in the town of Greenup. The Property Valuation Administrator is in Room 209 at 301 Main Street, phone (606) 473-9984, open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Mail to the sheriff goes to PO Box 318, Greenup, KY 41144, and the office answers at (606) 473-9833. The sheriff's tax page lets you pay online with your bill number and mailing address, and online payments carry convenience fees that go to the payment processor, not the sheriff. Refunds and account problems are handled in person at the sheriff's office, not by phone.

  • PVA: values, exemptions and appeals conferences, (606) 473-9984.
  • Sheriff: current-year payment, (606) 473-9833.
  • County Clerk: bills transferred after April 15, (606) 473-7394.
  • County Attorney: questions about the law behind the April 15 transfer, (606) 473-7855.

sections.h2: What is Greenup County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Greenup County lies along the Ohio River in the northeast corner of Kentucky, and it belongs to the Huntington-Ashland metropolitan area. The General Assembly created it in December 1803 from Mason County. Greenup is the county seat, Flatwoods is the largest city, and the other cities are Bellefonte, Raceland, Russell, South Shore, Worthington and Wurtland.

The river valley is flat and holds most of the industry, shops and housing, while the rest of the county rolls into Appalachian foothills with forest, farms and fishing spots at Greenbo Lake, Tygarts Creek and the Little Sandy River. US 23 follows the river through Russell, Flatwoods, Raceland, Wurtland, Greenup and South Shore and crosses to Portsmouth, Ohio on the U.S. Grant Bridge. The AA Highway, finished in 1995, runs west toward Maysville, and the Industrial Parkway links Wurtland to EastPark and Interstate 64.

Three school systems share the county: Greenup County Schools, Russell Independent and Raceland-Worthington Independent. Census QuickFacts supplies the housing numbers:

  • Population estimate for July 2025: 35,213, down 2.1 percent from the 2020 base.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 80.3 percent.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes (2020 to 2024): $134,000.
  • Median gross rent: $860. Median household income: $60,751. Persons in poverty: 16.7 percent.

sections.h2: What happens to a Greenup County tax bill after April 15?
sections.html:
It goes from the sheriff to the County Clerk, and the total starts climbing. The sheriff's page says April 15 is the last day to pay at the Sheriff's Office, and that bills turned over to the Clerk pick up fees that the original bill never showed. The sheriff's page cites House Bill 262 as the reason for the April 15 date.

The Department of Revenue prices out the stages for a $1,000 bill. It assumes a 4 percent sheriff commission, so your actual figures depend on the local rate.

Cost of a $1,000 Kentucky tax bill after transfer to the clerk (source: Department of Revenue example)
When paidTotal due
Within 5 business days of transfer$1,387.79
After the county attorney's first notice$1,611.30
After a second month of interest (May)$1,627.61
After newspaper advertising (June)$1,659.90
Bought by a third-party purchaser at the sale$1,704.21

Interest runs at 1 percent per month on the certificate. The clerk's sale of delinquent bills must fall 90 to 135 days after the transfer, which in a normal year means July 14 to August 28. Ask the Clerk's office for the third-party purchaser rules if you hold a bill that reaches the sale.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Greenup County assessment?
sections.html:
Go to the PVA's office for a conference, because the law lets only owners who have done that take an appeal to the board. The Greenup County PVA explains on its site that all property must be revalued every year and physically checked at least once every four years, so a value can shift without any change to your house.

  • Conferences happen during the 13 days of tax roll inspection that start on the first Monday in May, and the PVA's staff can see you earlier once notices are mailed.
  • After the conference you have until the close of business on the day after inspection ends to file the appeal at the County Clerk.
  • The local board hears cases 25 to 35 days after inspection closes and meets for no more than five days unless the state grants more.
  • Present records the board can weigh: your building costs, insurance policies, listings and photos. It turns down appeals without them.

The PVA's FAQ adds two reminders: keep your mailing address current with the office, and do not treat a missing bill or notice as a reason to skip payment. The PVA does not set tax rates, which come from the county, city and school boards that levy the tax.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption in Greenup County?
sections.html:
Yes, for homeowners 65 or older or totally disabled who own and live in the house. The 2025 and 2026 amount is $49,100, subtracted from assessed value. For a house at Greenup County's Census median of $134,000, taxable value would be $84,900.

Apply at the Greenup County PVA with a birth certificate, license, passport or other approved proof of age. A disability claim needs a classification from a federal agency or a retirement system, plus disability payments for the whole assessment period, and it must be renewed each year except for service-connected veterans and people who are permanently and totally disabled under Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

The PVA's FAQ still quotes a saving of about $280 for 2011, so ask the office for the current figure on your own parcel instead of relying on that old estimate.

sections.h2: What should I know about Greenup County taxes before selling?
sections.html:
Get payoffs from the right office, because the office depends on the date. Before April 15 the sheriff holds the bill. After that date the Clerk holds it, and the Clerk's delinquent tax page links the third-party purchaser information and application.

Kentucky treats the tax as the owner's personal debt as of January 1, and a lien from a delinquent bill outlasts a change of ownership for up to 11 years under KRS 134.420. A buyer's title search will find an unreleased lien, and the Clerk charges a recording and release fee for it.

Ask the closing agent how the current year's bill is split between you and the buyer, and make sure any bill still open at the Clerk is paid out of your proceeds. For a house with several years behind, a written payoff from the Clerk shows the full price of clearing the title.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Greenup County?
faqs.a: At the Greenup County Sheriff's Office through April 15, in person, by mail to PO Box 318, Greenup, KY 41144, or online. Call (606) 473-9833. Online payments carry processor convenience fees.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Greenup County assessment?
faqs.a: The Greenup County PVA at (606) 473-9984, in Room 209 of the courthouse at 301 Main Street. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: What happens to unpaid Greenup County tax on April 15?
faqs.a: The sheriff turns every unpaid bill over to the County Clerk. The Clerk adds fees that the original bill did not show, so call (606) 473-7394 for the total.

faqs.q: How much is the Greenup County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, for owners 65 or older or totally disabled. At the county median value of $134,000, the taxable amount drops to $84,900.

faqs.q: Can I get a refund from the Greenup County Sheriff over the phone?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff's page says refunds and account corrections must be requested in person at the Sheriff's Office, and staff do not handle them by phone.
